correctness.rationale: The original stochastic flip probabilities specialize to the exact count-chain probabilities. First-step recurrences produce the finite push double product. A uniform exponential upper/lower sandwich converges by Riemann sums to the explicit positive barrier for all nonconsensus initial counts. Nudging has positive count drift and harmonic-potential coupon bounds. All assumptions and endpoints are explicit; 352 exact rational linear systems, 2952 direct transitions and 1232 finite bounds were executed, with the infinity proof independent of finite tests.

value.rationale: The result distinguishes two externally influenced dynamics with identical eventual absorbing consensus but qualitatively different practical time scales, computes a positive rate for the exponential delay and gives sharp-order finite bounds for the fast rule. This resolves a mathematically natural long-time question left by simulation-based model introduction and explains metastable plateaus; it is not an arbitrary finite census.
